extracted.intended_audience: federal agency privacy officers, agency legal counsel, and members of the public who prepare or review Privacy Act systems of records notices (SORNs), matching program notices, and related rulemakings
extracted.subtask_short: privacy act SORN and matching notices
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for publishing, modifying, rescinding, and exempting Privacy Act systems of records (SORNs) and for issuing computer matching program notices, including required content, comment periods, OMB/EO compliance, and rulemaking steps. Targets agency officials preparing Federal Register notices and members of the public who comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act fair information practice principles / applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Privacy Act of 1974 establishes a code of fair information practice principles that govern Federal agencies' collection, maintenance, use, and dissemination of an individual's personal information. The Privacy Act applies to information that...","
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this standard to determine whether a system of records is covered by the Privacy Act (i.e., records about individuals maintained in a system of records). Ensure any collection/maintenance/use/dissemination decisions comply with the Act's fair information practice principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of System of Records Notices (SORNs) in the Federal Register
rubrics_metrics.description: "This action is necessary to meet the requirements of the Privacy Act to publish in the Federal Register notice of the existence and character of the system of records maintained by [agency]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must publish SORNs in the Federal Register to notify the public of the system's existence and character; notices should appear in the FR and include sufficient detail for public review and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required SORN content (system name, number, location, classification, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples shown in notices: "SYSTEM NAME AND NUMBER: ... SECURITY CLASSIFICATION: ... SYSTEM LOCATION: ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A SORN should include standard fields (system name and number, system location, categories of individuals, categories of records, authority, purpose, routine uses, storage, retrievability, safeguards, retention, system manager/contact, and security/classification). Provide complete metadata so readers can identify and understand the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment periods and submission procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices repeatedly state deadlines and how to submit comments: e.g., "Comments must be received by [date]" and "Comments on this matching notice must be received no later than 30 days after date of publication in the Federal Register."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify a clear comment deadline and provide detailed submission instructions (mailing address, email, online portal). Indicate whether the notice will become effective after the comment period unless contrary comments are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act exemptions and required rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Privacy Act allows Federal agencies to exempt eligible records in a system of records from certain provisions of the Act, including those that provide individuals with a right to request access to and amendment of records about the individual. If an agency intends to exempt a particular system of records, it must first issue a rulemaking pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(1)-(3), (c), and (e)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claiming exemptions (e.g., under 5 U.S.C. 552a(k)(1) and (k)(2)), agencies must promulgate a rule via notice-and-comment rulemaking that explains the exemptions, statutory basis, and justification (e.g., to protect classified or law-enforcement-sensitive information). Follow the cited APA provisions for procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Matching Program notice requirements and legal authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices reference: "Pursuant to the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended by the Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988, OMB Final Guidance Interpreting the Provisions of the Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988, and OMB Circular No. A-130... notice is hereby given of the conduct of [matching program]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching program notices must cite applicable statutes and OMB guidance, describe recipient and source agencies, state the purpose of the match, explain which data elements will be used (e.g., SSNs), and provide terms/duration and safeguards. Ensure compliance with the Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act and OMB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-108 / A-130 compliance, review, reporting, and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices cite OMB Circular No. A-108 (Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act) and OMB Circular No. A-130 (Management of Federal Information Resources). Some notices state modifications are to "align with new formatting requirements, published by OMB."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OMB A-108 and A-130 for periodic review, reporting requirements, required content and formatting of SORNs, and other agency responsibilities. Adopt any updated OMB formatting or procedural requirements when revising notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine uses required by Executive Order 14249 and OMB Memorandum M-25-32
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices state agencies "propose to add a routine use ... to implement requirements from Executive Order 14249, Protecting America's Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse, and OMB Memorandum M-25-32, Preventing Improper Payments and Protecting Privacy Through Do Not Pay."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing E.O. 14249 and M-25-32, add or modify routine uses in SORNs to permit disclosure to Treasury (or other designated entities) for Do Not Pay and improper payment prevention. Explain the routine use and identify the recipient(s) and purpose(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifying, rescinding, or consolidating SORNs (notice content and rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies give notice when they "propose to modify a current Privacy Act System of Records" or are "providing notice to rescind six Privacy Act SORNs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modifying or rescinding a SORN, publish a Federal Register notice that describes the changes or rescissions, provides reasons, and indicates how affected parties can comment. Include cross-references to the old notices and transitional arrangements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and applicability following public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Example language: "This modified SORN will become applicable following the end of the public comment period ... unless comments are received that result in a contrary determination."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify when the revised system or rule will take effect (e.g., after the comment period) and whether adverse comments will delay effectiveness. Clearly state the effective date or the condition under which it will become effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency regulatory updates to implement or reflect SORN exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: EOIR proposes to "update 28 CFR 16.83 consistent with the system of records' modifications to exempt this system of records from certain provisions of the Privacy Act ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When SORN exemptions require regulatory change (e.g., to agency Privacy Act regulations), propose and finalize regulatory amendments explaining the exemption rationale, statutory authority, and the changes to regulatory text. Invite public comment on such rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information and point-of-contact requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices include detailed contacts: e.g., names, titles, email addresses (privacy@agency.gov), phone numbers, mailing addresses, and directions for submission of comments or requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a named contact (privacy officer or system manager), telephone and email contact, and specific mailing addresses or online submission URLs for comments and inquiries. Include where FOIA/Privacy Act requests should be submitted and any online portals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching program operational details and purposes (examples: SSN verification, eligibility confirmation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples in notices: matching program "will enable AmeriCorps to verify the Social Security numbers of individuals ... to confirm that applicants meet eligibility requirements and to verify their statements regarding their citizenship status."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the matching notice describe the operational purpose (e.g., identity/SSN verification, eligibility determination), the categories of records to be matched, how results will be used, and safeguards to prevent misuse. State the agencies involved and the benefits/risks of the match.
